_note: Weights are relative — the scorer normalizes them. Filters are absolute and run before scoring. All profiles share one filter set so the columns stay comparable: anything below a 40% pass rate is not a solution, and flagged rows are disqualified outright.
_uncertain_field_note: Unusually, the Monte Carlo perturbs success rate rather than price. In this market prices are published and stable while pass rates are the contested claim — many are vendor self-reports on vendor-designed benchmarks. Perturbing the number everyone is motivated to inflate is the more honest stress test.

jod.label: Jod's browsing agent (stated goal)
jod.description: Don't get blocked, keep it cheap, keep the integration and compliance friction low.

cheapest.label: Pure cost
cheapest.description: Single-axis extreme, among options that actually clear the 40% bar.

max-success.label: Never get blocked
max-success.description: The opposite extreme: pass rate above all, cost irrelevant.

ethical.label: Consented IPs only
ethical.description: Weights sourcing ethics heavily. Worth running because the cheapest large pools are the ones with the worst consent stories.
